state_of_art: Haboush1975 is the solution; Sastry–Seshadri2011p415 gives a checked primary statement and alternative proof. The preface is dated27October1963, distinct from book publication1965.
why_open: This was Mumford’s published problem, not an undeveloped personal Grothendieck conjecture.
worth: No new proof project is needed; its value here is correct attribution and chronology.

title: Rational optimal destabilization
as_he_states: The GIT discussion asks for rational instability data.
plausible_today: For perfectk, k-rational unstablev and a Galois-invariant length, use Kempf’s optimal parabolic and rational cocharacters; imperfect fields require extra hypotheses.
state_of_art: The original Kempf preprint, circulated by fall1976 and digitized2018, Theorems6–7pp7–9, and Bate–Martin–Röhrle–Tange2013 Remark4.10 and Remark5.10 were checked.
why_open: The supplied text predates the checked solution; its presence in this folder does not establish a separate Grothendieck formulation.
worth: Worth only an exact field-hypothesis comparison if reused elsewhere.

title: The building-centre formulation in the preface
as_he_states: A finite isometry group of a convex set in the flag building is said to have a fixed point.
plausible_today: For a convex subcomplex of the appropriate spherical building, retain the alternative that it is a subbuilding; otherwise the stabilizing automorphisms have a fixed point.
state_of_art: The literal sentence is refuted here byQ8 on the whole rank-one SL2(C) building. Ramos-Cuevas2013 Conjecture1.1/Theorem1.2 and corollaries supply the modern qualified result.
why_open: The preface supplies an informal claim; no source explains the omitted alternative.
worth: The literal issue is settled by the counterexample; the useful task is editorial clarification.

title: The surface-moduli hope in the GIT preface
as_he_states: Develop stability and moduli for algebraic surfaces.
plausible_today: Choose a surface class, polarization, singularity convention and moduli functor before posing a modern theorem.
state_of_art: R-Q33 searched the preface and its invariant-theory successors. The retained broad hope has no uniquely matchable quantifiers, so no later surface-moduli theorem is assigned as its exact solution.
why_open: The preface presents a programme, not a stopped proof; no reason for abandonment is supplied.
worth: Worth only after narrowing the moduli problem; it is too broad for one research run.

title: Illusie’s proposed Riemann–Roch/Künneth appendix
as_he_states: The24February1968 letter proposes editorial work on a Riemann–Roch appendix and Künneth material.
plausible_today: Identify the intended version and correspondence before attributing a mathematical theorem to the letter.
state_of_art: R-Q35 searched the date, author, appendix and Künneth wording; the supplied letter is primary evidence, and the opened CSG catalogue verifies its exact author/date/cote. The outcome of the proposed editorial work was not located.
why_open: The letter records planned work; no outcome or reason for a change of plan is present.
worth: Worth a bounded bibliographic identification task, not a new theorem project.
